items.title: How much does JS bundle size delay first content under CSR?
items.description: Store A (client-rendered) can't show anything until the JS bundle downloads, parses, and runs on a mid-range phone over a 3G-ish connection. Drag the bundle size to see how first-content time scales — Store B's server-rendered page paints in about 1.1s regardless of bundle size, since it doesn't wait on any JS at all.
items.compute: const baseLatencySec = 1.1; const secPerKb = 0.00925; const csrSeconds = baseLatencySec + params.bundleSizeKb * secPerKb; return { csrSeconds: Math.round(csrSeconds * 10) / 10 };

outputs.label: Time until Store A shows anything

items.title: How much does adding interactive components widen the hydration gap?
items.description: The 'Add to cart' button looked ready at 1.1s but didn't actually respond until hydration finished — the uncanny valley of hydration. Under full hydration, every interactive component on the page (not just the one being tapped) has to be walked and wired up before any of them work. Drag the number of interactive components to see how much longer that takes.
items.compute: const baseFrameworkOverheadMs = 220; const msPerComponent = 18; const hydrationGapMs = Math.round(baseFrameworkOverheadMs + params.numInteractiveComponents * msPerComponent); return { hydrationGapMs };

items.title: How much does a slow data dependency delay blocking SSR?
items.description: In the reviewer's PR pushback, a plain SSR handler awaits every query before calling res.end() — so the 80ms product query gets held hostage by a slower recommendations query. Drag how slow that dependency is to see how long a visitor waits for anything at all. Streaming SSR flushes the header and product info as its own chunk the moment they're ready, so that first chunk stays at roughly 80ms no matter how slow the recommendations query gets — it just backfills the rest later over the same connection.
items.compute: const fastQuerySec = 0.08; const blockingTotalSec = Math.round((fastQuerySec + params.slowQuerySec) * 100) / 100; return { blockingTotalSec };

outputs.label: Time until anything is visible (blocking SSR)
